questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Uppsalahem took care of finding an empty room for me

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I prefered living closer to the city center, since all the student nations and activities take place there and it takes a while to go into the city from campus

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the only thing I needed to do was to pick up my SLU card, other than that, there wasn't any complicated registration process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My director of studies provided me with all the necessary information and contacts, which I could refer to if I had questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to enter all the classes I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as possilble and check the requirements

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took were definitely accomplishable also without former knowledge in these areas, but it made it easier to have a relevant background

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similiar, I think the differences in teaching methods lie more in the various subjects

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Governance of Natural Resources LU0093 HT2022
Soils of the world and sustainable water and soil management MV0215 HT2022

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master thesis in Environmental science, A2E EX0897 VT2023

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Soil science course because it touched many subjects from soil classification, to hydrologic calculations and sustainable water practices. I can recommend this course to everybody who is interested in the interface of soil sciences and hydrology

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Luckily there were no unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is very expensive, thus having a bike to move around is very important for a student friendly budget I think. Supermarkets were also not that cheap, so going to Lidl instead of ICA makes a huge difference.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The student union offered a large program of evening events and sport events, the latter I wasn't able to attend due to a sports accident but my colleagues did hikes and trips to Lapland, grillings, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the nations programs, ranging from free parties (with nation card) to fun game nights. There are so many offers and activities, I would just recommend to frequently check their fb pages and the nations guide online to not miss anything

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Following the river to the South, there is a beautiful lake to chill at when it gets warmer, there are lots of grill places, also in the forests, which is a great chance to go for a longer walk in the woods and then rest at the fire place. Due to my injury I wasn't able to explore a lot around the city and outside, but I can really recommend to cross the border to Norway and rent a place nearby the Fjords, for amazing hikes!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have the feeling, Uppsala is full of international students, especially in the dorm I lived in and at the nations, you'll find lots of open minded students, so it's not really hard to adjust. Moreover, Swedish people are very welcoming and speak English very well, thus it wasn't hard to adjust

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Naturally, through the courses you'll meet lots of Swedes which makes it easy to connect with them, then again in the nations and the student union, you'll be able to meets lots of them as well

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika and partying a lot

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think that the Swedish and Danish cultures are super different, so I can't think of any crucial points here

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Connecting to lots of people, and also attending very nice courses at a University considerably different than unis from where I come from (Austria)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the limited number of possibilites to explore my surroundings due to the accident, I also think it might have made more sense, to live together with students who also planned to stay for one year, instead of exeriencing all my roommates leaving after one semester and then getting to know new ones

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
